title: Merge Equal Neighbours Then Sink Zeros
statement:
You get an array nums of non-negative integers. Process it in two phases.

Phase 1. For i = 0, 1, …, n − 2, in this order, one index at a time: if nums[i] === nums[i + 1], double nums[i] and set nums[i + 1] to 0. Each step sees the changes made by earlier steps, and the scan never goes back.

Phase 2. Move every 0 to the end, keeping the other values in their order.

Return the resulting array.

examples.why: Index 0 merges the first two 2s into [4, 0, 2, 3, 3]. The third 2 now sits next to a 0, so it stays. Index 3 merges the 3s.
After the 4s merge into 8, the array is [2, 0, 8, 0, 8]. The two 8s are not neighbours during phase 1, so they never merge.
Nothing merges. The zeros sink and 5 moves to the front.

hints: Phase 1 is a single left-to-right scan; just do it exactly as written. The interesting part is phase 2.
Sinking zeros is the classic write-pointer move: copy every non-zero value to the next free slot at the front.
You can merge both phases into one loop: at each i, apply the merge rule, then if nums[i] is non-zero, write it to the front slot. Fill the rest with zeros.

explain.intuition:
The trap is reading phase 1 like the 2048 game, where merged tiles can merge again. Here each index is looked at once, in order, and the zero written at i + 1 stops any chain. So [2, 2, 2] gives one merge, not a cascade.

Phase 2 is the standard "move zeros" move: a write pointer w marks the next slot for a non-zero value. Since the merge at index i only touches i and i + 1, and nums[i] is final once that step is done, you can push nums[i] to the front in the same loop. The write pointer never passes the read pointer, so no unread value is overwritten.
steps: For each i from 0 to n − 1: if i + 1 < n and nums[i] === nums[i + 1], double nums[i] and zero nums[i + 1].
Then, if nums[i] !== 0, copy it to nums[w] and increase w.
Fill positions w … n − 1 with 0 and return nums.
pitfalls: Repeating the merge scan until nothing changes. The rule is a single pass, so [1, 1, 4, 4, 8] ends with two separate 8s.
Sinking zeros before merging, which lets values that were separated by a zero merge.
Sinking zeros by sorting or by removing and appending inside the loop, which breaks the order or costs O(n²).

solutions.title: Two separate phases
solutions.idea: Run the merge scan, then build a new array of the non-zero values followed by the zeros.

solutions.title: One pass with a write pointer
solutions.idea: Merge at i, then nums[i] is final: if it is non-zero, move it to the front slot right away.

followups: Implement one full 2048 row move: slide non-zero tiles left first, then merge each pair once. How does the order of the phases change the result?
Merge to the right instead, scanning from the end. Which pairs merge in [2, 2, 2]?
